validity.recommendation: Keep as a real, operating gas transmission trunk line; classification, operator, and endpoints are well supported. See separate spec concerns below for Length and Capacity, which need correction.
validity.researcher_notes: Started from the sheet's own cited sources (wiki_citations.json lists 2): (1) OPEC Annual Statistics Bulletin 2012 PDF, verified live (200, contains 'Libya'), but on full-text extraction (pdftotext) it is a generic country-level oil/gas statistics bulletin that never mentions 'Intisar', 'Intesar', or 'Brega' anywhere in the document — it does NOT name this pipeline and is not usable support for this row specifically (a generic-aggregate citation, per standing rule). (2) Zueitina Oil Co's own Arabic-language project page, 'Gas transfer project 103A [Intisar field] to the coastal network' (link_text/context confirm this). The live URL now 200s but is a bare React SPA shell with no content (the site was rebuilt; its public API only lists 4 current projects, none matching, and /api/v1/public/projects/34 returns 'Project item not found' -- the specific page is gone from the live site). Recovered the actual content via the Wayback Machine snapshot (2023-12-11), verified live and containing 'Zueitina', '207', and '42' -- this is the operative reference, not the dead live URL. The archived page is a genuine Zueitina Oil Company primary source (not GEM-derived, not wiki-derived) describing a real NOC-sponsored capacity-increase project that Zueitina oversees: piping natural gas via a 42-inch, internally/externally coated pipeline from 'field 103A' (part of the Intisar/Concession-103 complex Zueitina operates) to Al-Brega on the coast, feeding the coastal gas network toward both Tripoli and Benghazi branches -- exactly matching GEM's StartLocation ('Intesar Oil field'/Sirte Basin) and EndLocation ('Mersa Brega'/Al Wahat). This independently confirms the pipeline EXISTS as a real, named project (not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity) and is CLASSIFIED correctly as a major gas transmission trunk (not a gathering line) -- the article explicitly frames it as feeding heavy industrial complexes and power stations along the whole Libyan coast, at a target buildout of up to 1500 mmcf/d. Operator='Zueitina Oil Co' matches the source exactly (Zueitina is named as the company entrusted by NOC to oversee this project). Cross-checked against a second, unrelated independent source already used elsewhere in this batch (P1857's shard): a Feb 2026 Libya Herald article confirms Zueitina Oil Co is still the current, active operator of Field 103D (part of the same 103-series Intisar complex as 103A) -- reinforcing Operator=Zueitina Oil Co with a second, more recent independent source, and supporting Status=operating (the 103-field gas complex is described as active as of 2026). DUPLICATE check against the 30-pipeline roster: not a duplicate. It is distinct from P1857 (103D-103A, a short 41km internal field-to-field line), P1858/P6714/P6705 (Bu-Attifel-Intesar/Wafa-Mellitah, different origin fields), P3987 (Intisar-Sarir, same origin field but a different destination -- Sarir/Cyrenaica, not Brega), and P0482/P1866 (Defa-Brega/Nasser-Brega, different origin fields entirely). ConstructionYear=2010 is a caveat, not a hard confirmation: the archived article references a joint NOC/Zueitina meeting held 7 Feb 2010 and states the pipeline-laying phase was '85% complete' at time of writing (page last modified 2016-10-23, but that's a CMS timestamp, not a completion date) -- so 2010 is a reasonable year for when construction was underway/announced, but the source does not give a precise construction-start or completion year, so treat ConstructionYear as approximate.

validity.recommendation: Correct Length -- the operator's own project description gives ~207 km for this exact route (field 103A to Brega), not 333 km. Recommend revising LengthKnown to ~207 km pending a second confirming source, or at minimum flagging the current 333 km figure as unverified/likely wrong.
validity.researcher_notes: The Zueitina archived primary source is explicit and unambiguous: 'ينقل الغاز الطبيعي عبر أنبوب قطره 42 بوصة ... وبطول 207 كيلو متر تقريباً من حقل 103أ إلى البريقة على الساحل' = 'transports natural gas through a pipe 42 inches in diameter ... approximately 207 km long, from field 103A to Al-Brega on the coast.' This is the SAME route as GEM's Start/EndLocation (Intisar field/103A -> Mersa Brega) and the diameter (42in) matches GEM exactly, which makes this a strong, specific, on-point source -- yet it gives a materially different length (~207 km vs GEM's 333 km, a ~60% overstatement in GEM). Per the standing rule, a source merely mentioning the pipeline is not enough; this source actively disagrees with GEM's number on the same route, so this is a genuine spec concern, not a pass. I could not find a second independent source to adjudicate between 207 km and 333 km (search-engine scraping for this specific route/company returned no further hits), so I'm not proposing a fill of the corrected number -- just flagging GEM's current value as contradicted by the pipeline's own operator.

validity.recommendation: Correct Capacity/CapacityUnits -- GEM's '42.48 bcm/y' looks like a units-conversion bug, not a supported figure. Recommend recalculating from the source's mmcf/d targets (see notes) rather than keeping 42.48 bcm/y as-is.
validity.researcher_notes: The Zueitina source states the project's gas delivery targets in mmcf/day, not bcm/y: Phase 1 = ~250 million standard cubic feet/day; full build-out (all phases) = ~1500 million standard cubic feet/day. Converting for cross-check: 1500 mmcf/d x 28,316.85 m3/mmcf = ~42.475 million m3/day (Mm3/d) -- this is suspiciously exactly GEM's recorded Capacity figure of 42.48. That strongly suggests GEM's Capacity value was taken directly from this project's daily mmcf/d target, correctly converted to million m3/DAY, but then mislabeled with CapacityUnits='bcm/y' (billion m3/YEAR) instead of the correct daily unit. Annualizing correctly: 42.475 Mm3/d x 365 = ~15.5 bcm/y -- so even at the FULL eventual build-out target, capacity should read ~15.5 bcm/y, not 42.48 bcm/y (a ~2.7x overstatement as currently recorded); and Phase 1 alone (250 mmcf/d) is only ~2.6 bcm/y. This is a clear, quantifiable spec error, not just a rounding disagreement. I'm not proposing a specific corrected number as a confident fill because it's unclear whether the pipeline today (2026) has reached the full 1500 mmcf/d build-out or remains at an intermediate phase -- flagging for correction/verification rather than guessing.

summary: Existence and classification CONFIRMED via an independent Zueitina Oil Co primary source (archived, since removed from the live site) naming this exact 42in pipeline from field 103A/Intisar to Brega; Operator corroborated further by a 2026 Libya Herald article. Two spec concerns flagged: Length (GEM 333km vs source's ~207km) and Capacity (GEM's 42.48 bcm/y appears to be a units-conversion error against the source's mmcf/d targets, correct order of magnitude ~15.5 bcm/y at full build-out). UNRESOLVED: Length, Capacity, and Owner percentages -- no supporting ref proposed for GEM's current values on those three.
